rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the passed pawn on b4 runs to b8. Can the black king on g6 catch it in time?
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.e2: To answer without calculating move by move, draw the square of the pawn: its side runs from the pawn's square to the promotion square. Here it is White to move, and the pawn advances at once: count from b5.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.e3: With the pawn on its own, its king not nearby: if the opponent's king, on its turn, is inside the square or steps into it, it catches the pawn. If it stays outside, the pawn promotes.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.p: Play as White: the pawn or the king?
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes. After the advance, the square runs from b5 to e8, and the black king on g6 is outside it.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the pawn advance to b5: the square now runs from b5 to e8, and the black king on g6 is outside it.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.err.h1g2.1: The king goes to g2, far from the pawn, and the pawn stays on b4. The square still runs from b4 to f8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.err.h1g2.2: With this move Black has a resource: the king steps into the square on f5 and catches the pawn.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.err.h1g2.3: Back to the position: the move that takes the pawn out of the black king's reach is the pawn's own move.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.fora: With that move the pawn stays on b4 and the black king steps into the square. Look for the move that shrinks the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the pawn or the king?
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l1: Defence: the black king runs to f6, but the square of the pawn now runs from b5 to e8, and f6 is outside.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l2: Attack: the pawn advances to b6, and the square shrinks with it: now it runs from b6 to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l3: The king goes to e7, still one square outside the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l4: The pawn reaches b7, one square from promotion.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king reaches d7, but it does not control b8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex1.l6: The pawn reaches b8 and becomes a queen. When the pawn is to move, count the square from the square it goes to.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.e1: Defence: now with Black. The pawn on b5 runs to b8, and it is your king's move: the square runs from the pawn's square, from b5 to e8, and your king on f4 is outside it.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.p: Play as Black: with which move does the king step into the square?
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, the king steps into the square on e5. Now the pawn can no longer escape it.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.revela: The square is e5: it is the only one inside the square of b5 within the king's reach.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4f5.1: The king goes to f5, but the f-file is outside the square, which only reaches the e-file.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4f5.2: With this move White has a resource: the pawn advances to b6, and the square now runs from b6 to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4f5.3: Back to the position: look for the square inside the square of b5 that the king reaches now.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4e4.1: The king goes to e4, on the right file, but the 4th rank is below the square, which starts at b5.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4e4.2: With this move White has a resource: the pawn advances to b6, and the square now runs from b6 to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.err.f4e4.3: Back to the position: look for the square inside the square of b5 that the king reaches now.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.fora: With that move the king stays outside the square, which runs from b5 to e8. Look for its square within the king's reach.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the king must step into the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.l0: The king steps into the square on e5.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.l1: Attack: the pawn advances to b6, and the square shrinks: now it runs from b6 to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.l2: Defence: the king follows the pawn and stays inside the square, on d6.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.l3: The pawn reaches b7, one square from promotion.
rot.squareOfPawn.ideia.ex2.l4: The king comes to c7 and captures the pawn on b7 or on b8. Against a pawn on its own, on defence, stepping into the square on your turn is enough to catch the pawn.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.1: Attack: this position is from a game played on Lichess, near its end. The black king on g4 is right next to the pawn on g5, but behind it.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.2: Think before the move: capture the pawn on f2 or advance the pawn on g5? Draw the square of g6.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.3: The pawn advances to g6, instead of capturing on f2, which would let the black king capture the pawn on g5. The square runs from g6 to e8, and the black king on g4 is two ranks below it.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.4: Defence: the black king runs to f5, but being near the pawn is not enough: the king must be inside the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.5: The pawn reaches g7, and the square now runs from g7 to f8.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.6: The black king goes to e6, still outside the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.partida.7: The pawn becomes a queen on g8, with check. The pawn on f2 is still blocked by the white king on f1.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.1: Defence: with Black to move, the square of the pawn on g4 runs from g4 to c8. The king on b6 is one square away from it.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.2: The king steps into the square on c5.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.3: Attack: the pawn advances to g5, and the square now runs from g5 to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.4: Defence: the king follows the pawn to d6, inside the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.5: The pawn advances to g6, and the square shrinks: it runs from g6 to e8. The black king, on its turn, steps back into it.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.6: The king comes to e7, still inside the square.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.7: The pawn reaches g7, one square from promotion.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.8: The king comes to f7, next to g8, and captures the pawn.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.vez.9: With White to move, the pawn would go to g5 first, and the king on b6 would be outside the square. Whose move it is decides where you count from.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.1: Attack: with White to move, the square of the pawn on b4 is counted from b5, up to e8, and the black king on e6 is inside it. By the count, it catches the pawn.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.2: But your king on c6 stands next to the pawn's path and controls b7, c7 and d7: the black king cannot get in front of the pawn.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.3: The pawn advances to b5, and the white king on c6 keeps watching b7, c7 and d7.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.4: Defence: the black king goes to e7, heading for d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.5: The pawn advances to b6, protected by the white king on c6.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.6: The black king reaches d8, but the white king controls c7.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.7: The pawn reaches b7 and controls c8: the black king cannot reach the promotion square.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.8: The black king goes back to e7, with nothing to do.
rot.squareOfPawn.demos.excecao.9: The pawn becomes a queen on b8. The square count is for a pawn on its own: with its king nearby, first look at the squares that king controls.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Now with Black. The white king on e1 is inside the square of your pawn on f3, but your king is right next to it. Does the count hold here? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Your king went to g2 and controls f1 and f2: the white king, though inside the square, cannot get in front of the pawn, and the pawn promotes.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.f3: The pawn goes to f2 with check, but the white king goes to f1, in front of it, and blocks it. Meanwhile the white pawn on d5 runs.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3: The king goes to f4, heading for the pawn on d5, but it stays outside that pawn's square, which, with White to move, runs from d6 to f8: the white pawn runs to d8.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.rapido.enunciad: Black again. The white king on e2 is close to the square of your pawn on a4. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.rapido.fim: Being on move, the pawn advanced, and the square now runs from a3 to c1: the white king on e2 was left outside. With White to move, the king would step into the square on d2.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.rapido.err.h1g2: The king goes to g2, but the pawn stays on a4, and the white king steps into its square along the d-file.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.rapido.err.h1g1: The king goes to g1, but the pawn stays on a4, and the white king steps into its square along the d-file.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.corrida.enuncia: Black again. The white king on d5 is far from your pawn on h4. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.corrida.fim: With the advance, the square of the pawn ran from h3 to f1, and the white king was left outside it: the pawn ran to promotion.
rot.squareOfPawn.pratica.corrida.err.a6b: The king goes to b5, and the pawn stays on h4. The white pawn runs from c5 to c8, your pawn reaches h1 together with it, and both queens appear: the advantage is gone.
The king goes to b7, and the white pawn advances to c6 with check. Once your king gets out of check, the white king steps into your pawn's square on e4.
The king goes to b6, near the pawn on c6, but your pawn stays on h3. The white king goes to d6 and protects the pawn on c6, which also reaches promotion: the advantage is gone.
